selections.title: Strict TypeScript as the single application language
selections.decision_verbatim: Use strict TypeScript for domain, API, worker, transport schemas, metadata, generators, frontend, tests and governance. SQL remains the database language; configuration formats are not additional application languages.
selections.gist: Use strict TypeScript for domain, API, worker, transport schemas, metadata, generators, frontend, tests and governance.
selections.agent_case: The compiler is the primary self-correction loop. A single application language maximizes useful model context and reduces duplicated concepts.
selections.engineering_case: The browser is TypeScript regardless; using TypeScript on the backend removes a language instead of adding one. Shared concepts have one naming and testing culture.
selections.binding_constraints: Enable strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, useUnknownInCatchVariables, noImplicitReturns, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch, noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules and noEmit. Ban application any, unchecked domain casts and number-based authoritative money.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only on measured evidence that TypeScript cannot meet an accepted requirement after SQL, worker-process and bounded-service mitigations, or when AI generation is no longer the primary implementation mode.

selections.title: TypeScript 7 native compiler plus TypeScript 6 compatibility tooling
selections.decision_verbatim: Use TypeScript 7 for the fast command-line type check and TypeScript 6 through @typescript/typescript6 for type-aware tooling until the TypeScript 7 programmatic API is qualified.
selections.gist: Use TypeScript 7 for fast command-line type check and TypeScript 6 through @typescript/typescript6 for type-aware tooling until TypeScript…
selections.agent_case: TypeScript 7 materially shortens the red/green loop. The compatibility lane prevents speed from silently removing type-aware lint and ecosystem checks.
selections.engineering_case: The official TypeScript transition supports side-by-side use. Compiler parity is more important than choosing one prematurely.
selections.binding_constraints: Exact versions. Native and compatibility checks must both pass. Pin checker/builder parallelism; include a single-threaded parity lane. TypeScript or compiler upgrades are qualification events.
selections.revisit_trigger: When TypeScript 7.1+ exposes a stable programmatic API and all required tooling is qualified without the compatibility compiler.

selections.title: Node.js 24 LTS runtime
selections.decision_verbatim: Run API, workers, generators and governance on the exact patched Node.js 24 LTS baseline recorded in VERSION_BASELINE.json.
selections.gist: Run API, workers, generators and governance on exact patched Node.
selections.agent_case: Deep corpus, specific stack traces, broad library support and cheap local reproduction.
selections.engineering_case: The Node project recommends LTS for production. Runtime consistency lowers self-host and support variance.
selections.binding_constraints: Pin with .node-version or equivalent and assert process.version in CI. Do not adopt Current releases for production.
selections.revisit_trigger: At a scheduled LTS migration or security/support lifecycle event, followed by full qualification.

selections.title: pnpm workspaces and Turborepo
selections.decision_verbatim: Use pnpm workspaces as package authority and Turborepo only for deterministic task orchestration and cacheable dependency ordering.
selections.gist: Use pnpm workspaces as package authority and Turborepo only for deterministic task orchestration and cacheable dependency ordering.
selections.agent_case: One lockfile and explicit task graph give the agent a predictable repository loop.
selections.engineering_case: Efficient workspace installs, exact dependency graph and simple monorepo execution without a second application framework.
selections.binding_constraints: Exact packageManager field, frozen lockfile, no implicit install scripts unless allowlisted, no Nx/Bazel parallel authority.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only when repository-scale evidence shows the task graph or workspace model cannot meet build and governance requirements.

selections.title: Plain PostgreSQL 18 with PostgreSQL 17 compatibility floor
selections.current_evidence: E3-R for ledger kernel; stack selection E1
selections.decision_verbatim: PostgreSQL is the permanent financial-system contract. Primary qualification runs on PostgreSQL 18; every declared database behavior also passes on PostgreSQL 17 until the floor is explicitly raised.
selections.gist: PostgreSQL is permanent financial-system contract.
selections.agent_case: SQL is visible, mature, locally reproducible and produces constraint-specific errors. Critical invariants can live below generated application code.
selections.engineering_case: Deferred constraints, composite foreign keys, exact numeric, roles, RLS, SECURITY DEFINER, transactional outbox and reporting projections are native capabilities.
selections.binding_constraints: No provider-only SQL or SDK in the financial core. Run migrations, ledger spine, role/grant, concurrency and restore lanes separately on both majors.
selections.revisit_trigger: Never for the PostgreSQL contract; only the supported major floor and hosting profile change through qualification.

selections.title: node-postgres (pg) as canonical PostgreSQL driver
selections.decision_verbatim: Use node-postgres Pool and checked-out Client beneath Kysely and direct SQL. Every transaction uses the same client instance from BEGIN through COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
selections.gist: Use node-postgres Pool and checked-out Client beneath Kysely and direct SQL.
selections.agent_case: The driver is small, explicit and maps directly to PostgreSQL behavior. Transaction mistakes are easy to state and test.
selections.engineering_case: No hidden transaction abstraction. Type parsers can keep bigint, numeric and high-precision values as strings for owned conversion.
selections.binding_constraints: Never use pool.query inside a transaction. Own parsers for bigint/numeric/date-time. Parameterize data values and disallow dynamic identifiers outside reviewed helpers.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if a replacement proves equal PostgreSQL fidelity, smaller surface and stronger exact-type behavior under the full database suite.

selections.title: Kysely plus schema-derived code generation
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Kysely for ordinary typed queries; generate database types from the migrated PostgreSQL schema. Use reviewed SQL for ledger, migrations and advanced integrity operations.
selections.gist: Use Kysely for ordinary typed queries; generate database types from migrated PostgreSQL schema.
selections.agent_case: SQL-shaped code and compile-time schema drift provide a short, legible feedback loop.
selections.engineering_case: The database remains the source of truth and raw SQL is first-class rather than an unsafe escape hatch.
selections.binding_constraints: No hand-maintained database type authority. Codegen after migration. No Kysely plugin may hide tenant, transaction or money semantics.
selections.revisit_trigger: If Kysely introduces breaking instability or cannot express a measured query need without unsafe loss of types; direct SQL remains the fallback.

selections.title: Reviewed forward-only SQL migrations
selections.decision_verbatim: Use checksummed numbered SQL migrations. Migrations are applied by a dedicated migration credential and verified before application code generation.
selections.gist: Use checksummed numbered SQL migrations.
selections.agent_case: The complete schema and constraint errors are visible. No migration DSL or competing schema language must be inferred.
selections.engineering_case: Production changes remain reviewable, recoverable and independent of the query library.
selections.binding_constraints: No schema push in shared or production environments. Destructive/data-transforming changes escalate. Test empty install, upgrade from prior release, realistic data, dual majors and restore.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if another SQL-first migration runner improves evidence without becoming a second schema authority.

selections.title: Hono as a Node-only thin HTTP adapter
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Hono only through @hono/node-server. Route code parses transport, resolves actor/scope, calls one typed operation and maps Result to HTTP.
selections.gist: Use Hono only through @hono/node-server.
selections.agent_case: Small visible API and no decorator/DI magic. Binding the runtime removes multi-runtime ambiguity.
selections.engineering_case: The HTTP framework remains replaceable and contains no domain or persistence policy.
selections.binding_constraints: Node adapter only. Default router only. No Hono RPC as authoritative client contract. No business logic, ad hoc SQL or transactions in route handlers.
selections.revisit_trigger: On a breaking major or evidence that the thin-adapter boundary cannot be maintained.

selections.title: Zod 4 transport schemas and REST/OpenAPI contracts
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Zod 4 for every external boundary and @hono/zod-openapi as the sole API-schema path. Generate clients from OpenAPI; do not share server domain types over JSON.
selections.gist: Use Zod 4 for every external boundary and @hono/zod-openapi as sole API-schema path.
selections.agent_case: One schema produces runtime validation, static transport types and clear error paths.
selections.engineering_case: Transport/domain separation preserves bigint money, rational rates and explicit instants across a lossy JSON boundary.
selections.binding_constraints: Money minor units and rate components cross JSON as canonical integer strings. Validate request and response. Version authoritative endpoints. Hono RPC and hand-maintained duplicate client contracts are prohibited.
selections.revisit_trigger: If the approved Zod/OpenAPI path becomes unstable or cannot express required standards without a second authority.

selections.title: React 19.2 patched line with Vite 8.1 SPA
selections.decision_verbatim: Build a client-side React ERP delivered as static assets by Vite. Pin a patched React 19.2 line and prohibit all react-server-dom packages.
selections.gist: Build client-side React ERP delivered as static assets by Vite.
selections.agent_case: The browser/server boundary is a literal HTTP call. There are no Server Components, Server Actions, framework cache modes or file-location execution rules to confuse.
selections.engineering_case: An authenticated ERP gains little from SSR while static deployment is simple across managed and self-hosted profiles.
selections.binding_constraints: No Next.js, React Server Components or Server Actions. Dependency graph rejects react-server-dom-*. Exact React patch lives in the lockfile.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if a measured product requirement needs server rendering and a new architecture can preserve explicit authoritative boundaries.

selections.title: TanStack Router, Query, Table and Virtual; React Hook Form
selections.decision_verbatim: Use TanStack file-based routing only, TanStack Query for server state, Table/Virtual for dense grids, and React Hook Form integrated with the transport schemas.
selections.gist: Use TanStack file-based routing only, TanStack Query for server state, Table/Virtual for dense grids, and React Hook Form integrated with t…
selections.agent_case: Typed route/search state and headless explicit components make assumptions visible.
selections.engineering_case: ERP filters and drill-downs remain shareable URLs; grids remain license-safe and under design-system control.
selections.binding_constraints: One routing mode only. Generated route tree is generated output and drift-checked. Do not use generic un-narrowed router types that degrade TypeScript performance.
selections.revisit_trigger: If measured grid or route performance fails after documented narrowing and virtualization practices.

selections.title: Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn/ui source-owned components
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Tailwind CSS 4 and source-owned shadcn/ui components as the UI-system implementation.
selections.gist: Use Tailwind CSS 4 and source-owned shadcn/ui components as UI-system implementation.
selections.agent_case: The actual component source is in the repository; the agent reads and edits behavior rather than guessing a remote component API.
selections.engineering_case: No runtime design-system lock-in and full control of ERP density and accessibility.
selections.binding_constraints: UI components obey owned design tokens, accessibility gates and Storybook/component contracts. Avoid arbitrary one-off class drift.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only on measured maintainability, accessibility or performance failure.

selections.title: Standard OIDC boundary with Keycloak as reference provider
selections.decision_verbatim: Authentication integrates only through standard OIDC. Keycloak 26.7 is the reference self-hosted provider. AFENDA owns contextual business authorization.
selections.gist: Authentication integrates only through standard OIDC.
selections.agent_case: Identity-provider complexity is removed from generated application code; the integration surface is small and testable.
selections.engineering_case: SSO, MFA, federation and directory integration remain in a specialized identity system, while amount/entity/period/maker-checker authority stays under ERP doctrine.
selections.binding_constraints: No local password/auth framework in the core. Token validation and identity mapping are adapters. Keycloak roles do not replace AFENDA operation policies.
selections.revisit_trigger: Provider may change only after OIDC conformance, self-host, security, migration and operational qualification. Protocol boundary remains.

selections.title: Graphile Worker behind an owned JobQueue adapter
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Graphile Worker for generic at-least-once jobs such as email, PDFs, indexing and exports. Confine it behind one owned enqueue/worker adapter.
selections.gist: Use Graphile Worker for generic at-least-once jobs such as email, PDFs, indexing and exports.
selections.agent_case: The low-corpus library is reduced to a tiny local surface and current docs can be kept in context.
selections.engineering_case: It reuses PostgreSQL and avoids early queue infrastructure. It is not the authority for financial effect state.
selections.binding_constraints: Use public APIs only; never query private worker tables. Worker uses an appropriate direct/session-capable connection. Tasks are small, typed and idempotent.
selections.revisit_trigger: When measured throughput, isolation, retention or operational needs exceed the qualified adapter.

selections.title: AFENDA-owned transactional outbox for financial/statutory effects
selections.decision_verbatim: Create financial and statutory side effects through an owned durable state machine committed in the same database transaction as the source fact.
selections.gist: Create financial and statutory side effects through owned durable state machine committed in same database transaction as source fact.
selections.agent_case: The state transition is explicit and testable rather than hidden in queue retry behavior.
selections.engineering_case: Effectively-once business effect requires idempotency, acknowledgement, ambiguity handling and reconciliation beyond a generic job queue.
selections.binding_constraints: Generic queue executes work; it never defines financial truth. External calls never occur inside the posting transaction. States, attempts, fingerprints and operator actions are persisted.
selections.revisit_trigger: The implementation may move to another worker or workflow engine only if the owned state machine and evidence remain unchanged.

selections.title: S3-compatible object storage and PostgreSQL search first
selections.decision_verbatim: Use an owned S3-compatible storage port for documents and PostgreSQL full-text search plus pg_trgm for initial search.
selections.gist: Use owned S3-compatible storage port for documents and PostgreSQL full-text search plus pg_trgm for initial search.
selections.agent_case: Small explicit adapters and familiar SQL avoid early infrastructure complexity.
selections.engineering_case: Database stores immutable object metadata and digests; search remains a rebuildable projection.
selections.binding_constraints: No object-store vendor types outside the adapter. No OpenSearch or cache until measurements justify it. Search never becomes financial authority.
selections.revisit_trigger: On measured volume, linguistic or independent-scaling requirements.

selections.title: OpenTelemetry-first observability
selections.decision_verbatim: Instrument API, worker and browser with OpenTelemetry; export through an OpenTelemetry Collector to chosen backends.
selections.gist: Instrument API, worker and browser with OpenTelemetry; export through OpenTelemetry Collector to chosen backends.
selections.agent_case: One standard correlation model and specific runtime evidence improve agent diagnosis.
selections.engineering_case: Backend vendor remains replaceable while traces, metrics and structured operation attributes are consistent.
selections.binding_constraints: Initialize instrumentation before application code. Correlate actor, tenant/entity, operation, source and batch IDs without leaking money, personal data or secrets.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if the standard cannot meet a qualified operational requirement.

selections.title: Vitest, fast-check, StrykerJS and owned domain mutants
selections.current_evidence: E1 for stack; historical ledger evidence E3-R
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Vitest for the main test loop, fast-check for properties, StrykerJS for broad mutation and an independently maintained corpus of domain mutants for critical ERP invariants.
selections.gist: Use Vitest for main test loop, fast-check for properties, StrykerJS for broad mutation and independently maintained corpus of domain mutant…
selections.agent_case: Fast, specific failures enable self-correction; properties and mutants expose plausible but wrong generated code.
selections.engineering_case: Generic mutation score is secondary. Critical domain faults—money, scope, idempotency, time, locks, outbox and reversal—must have zero survival.
selections.binding_constraints: Tests may not be weakened without Reviewed approval. Critical mutant survival zero. Equivalent mutants require retained proof. Incident defects become permanent regression mutants.
selections.revisit_trigger: Tool may change only if fault sensitivity and evidence quality are preserved or improved.

selections.title: PGlite fast lane and Testcontainers PostgreSQL authoritative lane
selections.decision_verbatim: Use PGlite for fast deterministic SQL feedback and Testcontainers with real PostgreSQL for roles, concurrency, isolation, recovery and supported-major qualification.
selections.gist: Use PGlite for fast deterministic SQL feedback and Testcontainers with real PostgreSQL for roles, concurrency, isolation, recovery and supp…
selections.agent_case: Fast local checks preserve the generation loop; the server lane prevents WASM convenience from becoming false assurance.
selections.engineering_case: PGlite is single-connection; real role topology, multi-session races and restore behavior require actual PostgreSQL.
selections.binding_constraints: Concurrency-tagged tests cannot run only on PGlite. Testcontainers images are digest-pinned. Both PostgreSQL 18 and 17 lanes are independent.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if another local/server pair gives equal speed and stronger PostgreSQL fidelity.

selections.title: Playwright for end-to-end ERP workflows
selections.decision_verbatim: Use Playwright for browser qualification of the complete vertical slice and critical operator workflows.
selections.gist: Use Playwright for browser qualification of complete vertical slice and critical operator workflows.
selections.agent_case: Browser traces, screenshots and explicit actions provide a reproducible visible failure.
selections.engineering_case: The system must prove API, UI, database and audit behavior together, not only isolated functions.
selections.binding_constraints: At minimum: create invoice, approve, post, reverse, rebuild/view trial balance and inspect audit evidence. Trace retained on failure.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if a replacement provides equal cross-browser reliability and debugging evidence.

selections.title: Governed reporting schemas, read-only Metabase and CDC readiness
selections.decision_verbatim: Use afenda for authoritative data, reporting for governed projections and analytics for BI marts. Metabase is the optional read-only self-host BI profile. Design for CDC but create a slot only with a live monitored consumer.
selections.gist: Use afenda for authoritative data, reporting for governed projections and analytics for BI marts.
selections.agent_case: Clear schema boundaries and SQL projections are visible and locally testable.
selections.engineering_case: BI is language-independent. Core dimensions use entity-scoped columns/FKs; analytical extension dimensions use normalized bridges; JSONB remains opaque metadata.
selections.binding_constraints: BI role has read-only schema access. No posting EXECUTE. CDC slot requires owner, consumer, lag monitoring, WAL budget, snapshot and removal procedure.
selections.revisit_trigger: BI tool may change; reporting schema contract and CDC safety remain.

selections.title: OCI containers and Docker Compose first
selections.decision_verbatim: Ship web, api, worker, PostgreSQL, Keycloak, optional object storage, Metabase and OpenTelemetry Collector as digest-pinned OCI profiles; Docker Compose is the first self-host profile.
selections.gist: Ship web, api, worker, PostgreSQL, Keycloak, optional object storage, Metabase and OpenTelemetry Collector as digest-pinned OCI profiles; D…
selections.agent_case: The full failure surface is reproducible locally without a cloud control plane.
selections.engineering_case: Self-hostability and provider portability are product requirements; Kubernetes is a later deployment profile, not an application dependency.
selections.binding_constraints: After dependency and image acquisition, verification runs with external egress denied. Fresh-airgapped installation is not claimed without an artifact mirror. Helm later only after demand.
selections.revisit_trigger: Add HA/Kubernetes profiles on customer/SLA evidence, not fashion.

selections.title: Modular monolith in one repository
selections.decision_verbatim: Build one modular application with deployable api and worker processes. Domain modules expose commands, queries, events and read contracts—not repositories, tables or internals.
selections.gist: Build one modular application with deployable api and worker processes.
selections.agent_case: The agent can inspect end-to-end behavior without distributed-service context loss.
selections.engineering_case: Strong boundaries without the operational cost, partial failure modes and data ownership complexity of premature microservices.
selections.binding_constraints: Feature-first packages, root public APIs, dependency graph checks, no cross-module data writes, no transport concerns in domain packages.
selections.revisit_trigger: Extract a service only on measured scaling, isolation, deployment or ownership evidence with a stable contract.

selections.title: Functions, immutable data and explicit capability objects
selections.decision_verbatim: Domain/application operations use functions, immutable data and explicit dependency objects. Classes are allowed only at adapters where a library requires them and behavior remains visible.
selections.gist: Domain/application operations use functions, immutable data and explicit dependency objects.
selections.agent_case: An operation is understandable from its input, dependencies, control flow, result and tests.
selections.engineering_case: Avoids hidden proxy transactions, decorator DI, inheritance state and service-locator coupling.
selections.binding_constraints: Forbidden: class-based domain inheritance, decorator-driven DI, reflection, service locators, implicit transactions, ambient global state and runtime module discovery.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only if a pattern proves equally visible and mechanically enforceable.

selections.title: AI as proposal-only capability
selections.decision_verbatim: AI may extract, classify, explain, match and propose structured changes. It never holds a ledger capability and cannot create an authoritative financial fact.
selections.gist: AI may extract, classify, explain, match and propose structured changes.
selections.agent_case: Structured Zod outputs keep AI behavior inside the same TypeScript feedback and validation system.
selections.engineering_case: Model uncertainty, provider change and prompt behavior remain outside the accounting authority. Human-approved operations own posting.
selections.binding_constraints: Store model/prompt/input provenance and confidence. AI writes proposals only. No autonomous posting, payment release, period close or statutory submission.
selections.revisit_trigger: Automation may increase only after qualified accuracy, control, audit and regulatory evidence; ledger authority remains human-governed.

selections.title: Declarative/trusted extensions first; untrusted code out of process
selections.decision_verbatim: Phase-one extensions are declarative fields, view slots, document types, trusted version-controlled policies and after-commit hooks. Untrusted executable code runs only in a separate isolated process/service with capability-scoped APIs.
selections.gist: Phase-one extensions are declarative fields, view slots, document types, trusted version-controlled policies and after-commit hooks.
selections.agent_case: Avoids low-corpus, security-sensitive in-process sandbox semantics.
selections.engineering_case: The operating-system/process boundary is more auditable than a clever JavaScript isolate with direct database reach.
selections.binding_constraints: No direct database credential for untrusted extensions. No execution inside posting. Time, memory, network, data and failure scopes are declared.
selections.revisit_trigger: Only after a separately qualified extension-host design and threat model.

controls.name: TypeScript native/compat parity
controls.required_outcome: TypeScript 7 native check, TypeScript 6 stable-order compatibility check, and type-aware lint all pass.

controls.name: Strictness and no-any
controls.required_outcome: Strict compiler options enabled; application any and unchecked casts are rejected.

controls.name: Authoritative money type safety
controls.required_outcome: No JavaScript number in authoritative money contracts or code paths; JSON money uses canonical integer strings.

controls.name: Exact toolchain pins
controls.required_outcome: Runtime, compilers, package manager, dependencies and lockfile are exact and CI-verified.

controls.name: Module boundaries
controls.required_outcome: Dependency graph forbids domain-to-adapter imports, internal subpaths and cycles.

controls.name: Provider-neutral financial core
controls.required_outcome: No managed-vendor SDK or provider-only SQL primitive in ledger and database kernel paths.

controls.name: Dual PostgreSQL major qualification
controls.required_outcome: Migrations and authoritative database controls pass separately on PostgreSQL 18 and PostgreSQL 17.

controls.name: Single-client transaction rule
controls.required_outcome: Every transaction uses one checked-out node-postgres client from BEGIN through COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

controls.name: Exact database type parsing
controls.required_outcome: bigint/numeric/date-time authoritative values are parsed under owned rules, not implicit JavaScript coercion.

controls.name: Schema-derived Kysely types
controls.required_outcome: Kysely types regenerate from migrated PostgreSQL; drift fails CI.

controls.name: Migration integrity
controls.required_outcome: Migration checksums, ordering and review status are verified; no schema push in shared or production environments.

controls.name: Hono runtime and contract path
controls.required_outcome: Only @hono/node-server and @hono/zod-openapi appear in authoritative API code; Hono RPC is prohibited.

controls.name: One frontend routing mode
controls.required_outcome: TanStack file-based routing only; generated route tree drift fails CI.

controls.name: No React Server Components
controls.required_outcome: No react-server-dom-* dependency and no Server Components/Server Actions architecture.

controls.name: OIDC boundary
controls.required_outcome: Authentication uses standard OIDC; contextual ERP authorization remains inside AFENDA operations.

controls.name: Queue adapter boundary
controls.required_outcome: Graphile Worker appears only behind the owned JobQueue adapter; private worker tables are not queried.

controls.name: Financial outbox required
controls.required_outcome: Every authoritative external financial/statutory effect is created through the owned outbox state machine in the source transaction.

controls.name: Critical mutation survival zero
controls.required_outcome: All critical TypeScript and domain mutants are killed; exceptions require time-boxed Owned approval.

controls.name: Concurrency lane enforcement
controls.required_outcome: Concurrency-tagged tests are rejected on PGlite and run on real multi-session PostgreSQL.

controls.name: Browser workflow gate
controls.required_outcome: Playwright verifies the vertical ERP flow and audit evidence before release.

controls.name: Read-only BI boundary
controls.required_outcome: BI role has SELECT only on reporting/analytics schemas and no posting-function execution.

controls.name: CDC slot safety
controls.required_outcome: No logical replication slot exists without a named live consumer, lag alert, WAL budget and removal procedure.

controls.name: Reproducible self-host profile
controls.required_outcome: After lockfile dependencies and digest-pinned images are acquired, the stack and verification run with external egress denied.

controls.name: Explicit application architecture
controls.required_outcome: No decorator DI, service locator, class-based domain inheritance, implicit transaction or hidden runtime module discovery.

controls.name: AI cannot post
controls.required_outcome: AI identities and proposal workers cannot call or insert into the ledger; human-approved operation path remains mandatory.

controls.name: Extension isolation
controls.required_outcome: Untrusted executable extensions have no in-process execution and no direct database credential.

controls.name: Stack authority integrity
controls.required_outcome: STACK.md hash matches STACK.sha256 and every selection/control has complete metadata.

explicit_rejections.reason: Strong conventional engineering but violates the one-language, fast-feedback, vibe-code-primary constraint.

explicit_rejections.rejected_option: Next.js, React Server Components and Server Actions
explicit_rejections.reason: Invisible server/client and cache semantics on authoritative code; RSC dependency is explicitly prohibited.
Hidden provider resolution, lifecycle and reflection.
API-churn risk under the project’s version-mixing criterion.
Second schema language and migration authority outside reviewed SQL.
Weakens explicit operation identity, idempotency and audit semantics.

explicit_rejections.rejected_option: Bun or Deno as primary runtime
explicit_rejections.reason: Less stable primary corpus and additional runtime-specific behavior.

explicit_rejections.rejected_option: Microservices, Kafka, Redis or Temporal on day one

explicit_rejections.reason: Breaks plain PostgreSQL portability and self-host qualification.
Bypasses operation contracts, evidence, idempotency and authorization.
Security boundary is too subtle for the project’s generation model.
Unversioned behavior outside code review and verification.
Model output cannot become authoritative financial substance.

escape_hatches.title: CPU-bound workloads
escape_hatches.text_verbatim: Use, in order: **set-based SQL**, then **Node worker processes/worker threads**, then a **bounded specialist service** only after profiling proves CPU—not database or I/O—is the limiting factor. The specialist service owns no ledger credential and returns a proposal/result through a narrow versioned contract.
escape_hatches.gist: Use, in order: set-based SQL, then Node worker processes/worker threads, then bounded specialist service only after profiling proves CPU—no…

escape_hatches.title: Concurrency
escape_hatches.text_verbatim: Concurrency remains an Owned surface. Posting, period close, numbering, idempotency, valuation and restatement coordination live in one small package. Nothing passes without real multi-session PostgreSQL tests, killed lock-order/isolation mutants, whole-transaction retry evidence and an independent final-state oracle.

escape_hatches.title: Untrusted extensions
escape_hatches.text_verbatim: Do not build an in-process sandbox initially. Untrusted code runs in a separate killable process/service with no database credential and a capability-scoped API. Phase-one extensions remain declarative or trusted/version-controlled.
escape_hatches.gist: Do not build in-process sandbox initially.

escape_hatches.title: Future service extraction
escape_hatches.text_verbatim: A module may become a service only after a measured scaling, isolation, deployment or ownership requirement exists and the stable contract, data ownership, failure handling and reconciliation are already executable in the monolith.
escape_hatches.gist: module may become service only after measured scaling, isolation, deployment or ownership requirement exists and stable contract, data owne…

version_policies: Release lines are selected here; exact patches and image digests are machine authority.
Agents may not upgrade Node, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, React, Vite, Keycloak or constitutional dependencies.
A runtime/compiler/database major or qualified toolchain change requires representative regeneration, semantic diff, full applicable controls and explicit approval.
Security patch upgrades are expedited but still run affected qualification.
`package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.node-version`, container digests and CI image constants must agree with `VERSION_BASELINE.json`.
No unbounded `latest`, caret or tilde range is allowed for constitutional dependencies in the committed application manifest.

architecture_constraints.repository_tree:
/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/                 # React + Vite
│   ├── api/                 # Hono Node adapter
│   └── worker/              # Graphile Worker adapter + outbox executor
├── packages/
│   ├── domain/              # pure types, value objects and rules
│   ├── operations/          # commands and queries
│   ├── contracts/           # Zod + OpenAPI transport schemas
│   ├── db/                  # Kysely types and transaction adapters
│   ├── errors/              # canonical Result/failure contracts
